findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, defeating the purpose of lazy loading
findings.body: All entries of the appStore object are built with `import("./appname")` calls placed directly inside an object literal. Because this literal is evaluated once, synchronously, as soon as the module is first loaded, every one of the ~26 dynamic import() calls fires immediately and in parallel, exactly like the previous static imports. None of them is deferred until the specific app is actually needed. As a result, every consumer (getCalendar, videoClient, handleCancelBooking, etc.) still triggers loading of all app packages up front, but now each access additionally requires an `await`, adding complexity and promise-resolution overhead without achieving true on-demand/lazy loading. To actually defer loading, each entry would need to be a function returning the import (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`), invoked only when that specific app is required.

findings.title: Example comment references a non-existent module path
findings.body: The comment `// example: import("./example"),` doesn't match the actual folder name. The previous code's commented-out import referenced `"./_example"` (with a leading underscore), which is the real folder used to keep the example app excluded from the registry. If a developer later copies this comment to register a new app, it will point at a module that doesn't exist.

findings.title: forEach with async callback no longer reliably initiates calendar deletion before later steps run
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` now calls `await getCalendar(...)` inside the callback (previously `getCalendar` was synchronous). Array.prototype.forEach never waits for promises returned by its callback, so once getCalendar became async, the loop body suspends at the `await` and the surrounding `forEach` call returns before any of the calendar deletion requests are even issued. Execution then proceeds to `await sendRequestRescheduleEmail(...)` and the function returns `true`, with no guarantee that the calendar/video deletion calls have started, let alone completed. Previously, since getCalendar was synchronous, the deletion request was synchronously kicked off inside the loop before any later code executed. Additionally, the enclosing try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch errors thrown inside these detached async callbacks, so failures become unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged. Net effect: a reschedule can report success and send the reschedule email while the old calendar/video events are still pending deletion or were never actually requested to be deleted in time.

findings.title: forEach with async callback no longer reliably initiates calendar deletion before later steps run
findings.body: Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` now awaits the newly-async `getCalendar(...)` inside the callback, but forEach does not wait for the returned promises. The loop no longer guarantees the calendar/video deletion requests are even started before the function continues to send the reschedule email and returns. The surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections raised inside these detached async callbacks.

findings.title: requestReschedule forEach no longer waits for (or even reliably starts) calendar/video deletion before sending the reschedule email and webhooks
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` was previously a synchronous callback that called `getCalendar` synchronously, so the deletion request was always issued inside the loop before the mutation continued. Now `getCalendar` is awaited inside the async callback, and since forEach ignores the promises returned by async callbacks, the deletion requests may not even be initiated before the code proceeds to `await sendRequestRescheduleEmail(...)` and subsequently dispatches BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks. This changes the ordering guarantees of the reschedule flow and can leave stale calendar/video events behind while users are already notified of the reschedule.

findings.title: Nested forEach(async) race widened by newly-async getCalendar, risking dropped deletions from final Promise.all
findings.body: In the recurring-event branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` is not awaited by the surrounding code. `apiDeletes` is only consolidated and awaited much later via `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line ~652), relying on other intervening awaits in the function to give these detached async callbacks enough time to push their results. Converting the previously-synchronous `getCalendar` call to `await getCalendar(credential)` adds an extra asynchronous hop before each callback even starts its inner loop, widening the race window during which `apiDeletes` may not yet contain the recurring-booking's calendar deletion promises when the final Promise.all executes, risking recurring-booking calendar events that are never actually deleted on cancellation.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters resolves credentials sequentially instead of in parallel
findings.body: The rewritten `getVideoAdapters` uses a `for...of` loop with `await appStore[appName as keyof typeof appStore]` inside, resolving each credential's app module one at a time rather than concurrently (e.g. via `Promise.all`). For bookings with multiple video credentials this unnecessarily serializes independent promise resolutions on every call to createMeeting/updateMeeting/deleteMeeting/getBusyVideoTimes, adding avoidable latency compared to a parallelized implementation.

findings.title: No tests cover the new async appStore / getCalendar / getVideoAdapters behavior
findings.body: This PR converts appStore's values to Promises and makes getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, and getCalendarCredentials asynchronous, touching booking cancellation, rescheduling, calendar/video event creation, and payment flows across many files. Several of these changes introduce race conditions around unresolved promises inside `Array.prototype.forEach` callbacks (see findings on vital/wipemycalother reschedule.ts, bookings.tsx, and handleCancelBooking.ts). No unit or integration tests were added or updated to verify that calendar/video events are still correctly created, updated, and deleted during these flows after the conversion, so these regressions would not be caught by CI.
